                    ### Question
                    A 45-year-old woman gravida 1, para 1, comes to the physician because of a 2-month history of a right breast lump and a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss. She has not had any breast pain or nipple discharge. She had right breast mastitis 10 years ago while breastfeeding but has no other history of serious illness. A mammogram shows a density with calcifications in a star-shaped formation in the same location of the mass. Histological examination of a biopsy specimen from the breast mass is most likely to show which of the following?

                    ### Options

opb. Disorganized nests of glandular cells with surrounding fibrosis
opc. Large, pink-staining cells in the epidermis
opd. Orderly rows of monomorphic cells that do not stain with E-cadherin
ope. Infiltration of ductal cells blocking the dermal lymphatics

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):

The biopsy findings most likely reflect disorganized nests of glandular cells with surrounding fibrosis, which is characteristic of invasive ductal carcinoma. The reasoning chain for this option aligns with consensus, as the presence of a firm mass and calcifications indicates malignancy, and the histological features support the diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma. Other options, such as dilated ducts with necrotic centers or infiltration of ductal cells blocking dermal lymphatics, are less consistent with the typical presentation and findings of this case. Therefore, the most likely histological finding is disorganized nests of glandular cells with surrounding fibrosis.
